name: Tempest Ridge
geological_features: Atmospheric ridgeline of compressed gas forming a permanent raised band
Sulfuric acid cloud layers in the upper atmosphere
Liquid helium rain in the deep atmosphere
Dense core of compressed metallic elements
description: Tempest Ridge is a massive gas giant with a toxic atmosphere dominated by sulfuric compounds that tint its cloud bands in sickly yellows and greens. Its most unusual feature is a permanent atmospheric ridgeline, a zone of compressed gas that circles the planet like a raised scar, rising visibly above the surrounding cloud tops. The ridge spawns violent storms on both flanks.

The planet's appearance is unsettling, its color palette evoking disease and decay. Sulfuric acid rain falls in the upper atmosphere, evaporating before reaching the denser layers below. The atmospheric ridge distorts the usual banded pattern, creating a visual asymmetry that makes Tempest Ridge look somehow wrong, as if the planet is deformed.

The atmospheric ridgeline has no counterpart in any other known gas giant. Modeling suggests it may be maintained by an unusual internal heat distribution, possibly related to the core's composition. Deep atmospheric probes have detected liquid helium precipitation at extreme depths, a phenomenon that may contribute to the ridge's stability through convective feedback.

Tempest Ridge's sulfuric atmosphere corrodes harvesting equipment rapidly, making fuel extraction more expensive than at comparable gas giants. The planet sees limited commercial activity, serving primarily as a navigation landmark and scientific curiosity. Its moons, however, host several mining operations that benefit from the giant's gravitational influence on local asteroid orbits.
